jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: The Human ATM
jokes.joke: I saw a billionaire stop to watch a street musician. The guy finished his song, held out his hat, and the billionaire dropped in a dollar. I thought, wow, even billionaires tip badly. Then the musician pulled out his phone, took a picture of the billionaire, and said, 'For five bucks, I'll delete it.'

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Open Mic Parade
jokes.joke: I used to be a street performer. Juggling, mostly. The problem was my act was temperamental. Some days I'd juggle five balls beautifully, and other days I'd drop one and have a full breakdown on the sidewalk. Honestly, people tipped way more for the breakdown. So now I just stand there holding one ball, sobbing. It's called 'minimalist,' and I've never made more money.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Helpful Local
jokes.joke: I have one of those sweet, innocent faces, so tourists constantly stop me for directions. The problem is, I have absolutely zero sense of geography, but an overwhelming desire to be helpful. So I just give a warm, welcoming smile, point confidently down the avenue, and send a minivan full of tourists straight into the municipal water treatment plant.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Living Statue
jokes.joke: I tried the living-statue street performer gig last summer. Stand still, collect tips, easy money. Problem is I'm temperamental. So the second a tourist snaps a selfie without dropping a coin, I break character, point straight at them, and bark, "My stillness isn't free!" Then freeze again like nothing happened. The tips improved. The confusion was priceless.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Celebrity Upgrade
jokes.joke: I knew I wasn't ready to be rich and famous when a guy playing guitar on the sidewalk opened a case full of cash and I got jealous. I stood next to him with my coffee hoping people would tip me for listening. One tourist dropped a dollar in my cup and said, you're not very good at this. I said, compared to my day job, I'm crushing it.

scores.comment: Clear escalation from juggling to monetizing emotional breakdowns. The one-ball image is amusing, but the minimalist punchline is predictable and only mildly funny.
Relatable setup, but the water treatment plant feels arbitrarily selected rather than comically inevitable. The ending offers an absurd destination without a strong punchline.
The angry living statue creates a recognizable comic contradiction. 'My stillness isn't free!' is the strongest moment, but the two sentences afterward dilute its impact.

The accidental career as a paid spectator is a fresh, relatable premise with natural first-person delivery. The final comparison to the day job lands, though it lacks the sharp surprise needed for a higher laugh score.
Clear premise and a real turn: the busker flips into a shakedown. The last line works but reads slightly like a stock joke. The 'tip badly' beat is a flat middle.
Confident wrong directions leading to the water treatment plant is a good image, but the minivan escalation is predictable. 'Innocent' is used as a concept; 'bad information' is implied well.
Strong stage premise: the statue breaking character to demand payment. 'My stillness isn't free' is a clean punchline. The final two lines add a mild explanatory tail that slightly dilutes the peak.
Jealousy of a busker is a workable idea, but the turn is muddled. 'Crushing it' compared to a day job is vague and doesn't land. Rhythm is loose and the ending is not clearly the funniest beat.
The logic of the punchline falls flat; there's no clear reason a billionaire would pay to delete a random photo of himself.
Excellent escalation and a very funny, natural stand-up persona. The 'minimalist' turn works perfectly.
A strong visual premise, but 'the confusion was priceless' is a cliché closer that dilutes the actual punchline.
Good self-deprecating stand-up rhythm. The coffee cup misunderstanding builds to a solid, relatable punchline.
Clean setup and blackmail snap work, but the rich-cheap premise stays familiar and the laugh stays mild.
Strong escalation from temperamental drops to deliberate sobbing minimalism; the final image carries a real comic payoff.
Specific destination gives a clear visual, yet the innocent-bad-directions shape is well-worn and the laugh remains polite.
Premise is clear but the turn is soft and the final line only restates self-deprecation without a sharper snap.
Strong reversal with the musician extorting the billionaire; clear setup and payoff.
Good escalation from juggling failure to monetized breakdown; amusing but somewhat predictable.
Clear premise and visual payoff; the wrong-directions idea is familiar, though the destination adds punch.
Nicely observed character behavior, strong image, and the freeze-again tag lands cleanly.
